$comment: The values a consumer may set in its nen/workflow.json, nen/gates.json or nen/contract.json that a Hatsu skill reads and that either carry a canon default safe to write out or are needed by a skill, with the default its readers apply when it is absent. The maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-01 (docs/ROSTER.md § Rulings of 2026-10-01): the configuration files show every optionally settable value at its default, a fixed-set value carries a `$<key>` sibling listing its options, and a skill that needs a value nobody has set guides the maintainer through setting it instead of stopping. scripts/config_values.sh is the only reader: `diagnose` reports, `fill` writes the defaults and annotations (behaviour-neutral by construction), `need --skill <s>` lists what a phase cannot run without, `set` writes one chosen value. Each `default` is the one canon already states, cited in `source`, and `check-catalogue` holds it against docs/WORKFLOW.md's key tables. Two kinds of value are not listed, because writing a snapshot would stop it following its source: one derived at run time (iteration.lane from project.defaultLane, reports.timeZone from the host), and one whose default a reader resolves from a Hatsu canon file only when the key is absent (gates.json round_policy, sharingan § 6 and contracts/round_policy.default.json; nen reads the same keys from v0.21.0 and enforces no ceiling it was not given). LISTED BUT HATSU-OWN: the workflow.intake.challenger.* rows (domain intake) are Hatsu's own policy, read from Hatsu's checkout only and gated by `when: nen/workflow.json#intake`, so fill never writes them into a consumer; a consumer's own intake block is tolerated and never read by emperor-time. NOT LISTED, each for a stated reason (a snapshot or a guess would change behaviour, or nen owns the key): values derived at run time (iteration.lane, reports.timeZone; profile.default, which nen derives from profile.allowed, is listed for its options and never given a default); values a reader resolves from a Hatsu canon file only when absent (gates round_policy.minRounds/.maxRounds, nen's keys from v0.21.0); values nen also reads whose built-in default may differ from the skills' (commits.allowedAttributionTrailers, commits.forbiddenTrailers, commits.runTrailer, futon.advanceGo, gates round_policy.stallMinutes, gates version); structural blocks whose shape is the repository's own (models, reports.sections, gates delivery, dependabot_carve_out, checks.excluded, round_quorum, default_approvers, base_reviewers -- Hatsu's check_exclusions and reviewer_fallback are retired, ruling 2026-10-04, and nen v0.21.0 refuses both); and nen/repos.json, nen/labels.json and the YAML files, which tenkai's other items own. Row fields: `kind` enum (a fixed set, `options` lists it) | subset (a list drawn from a fixed set, annotated `any of:`) | open (any value of its shape) | external (needs a step on an outside platform, `setup` names it) | secret-env (an environment-variable NAME, never the secret); `requiredBy` the skills that cannot run while it is unset; `ask` adoption (Tenkai asks for it) | on-use (only some repositories need it: Tenkai offers it, and the first skill in `requiredBy` to run asks then); `when` a <file>#<path> that must be non-empty for the row to apply; `candidatesFrom` a <file>#<path> whose keys are the picker's options; `nullIsAnswer` a null its readers treat as a deliberate answer (ask on each call), never outstanding; `choice: maintainer` a value WORKFLOW § 4 says is typed, never picked (row missing-maintainer-choice): candidates shown for reference, none starred; `sourceTable: false` a default documented in docs/WORKFLOW.md's prose rather than its key tables, which `check-catalogue` then holds to a line naming the key; `nonProductionTarget` `set` refuses a target whose `why` does not read non-production or that is not marked project.targets.<name>.nonProduction: true (nen 0.21+ FAILs schema check without it, zheref/nen#300); `landsByPR` a value that lands through its declaration PR before it runs, so the phase does not resume on it. `nen schema check` stays the authority on each file's validity; this catalogue is Hatsu's list of what Hatsu reads.

The owner/name of the canon handbooks repository a port ruling lands in (hatsu:bankai-rule § 2): its ports family is read at the consumer's pinned tag and authored in a separate clone at the cache path, never the canon checkout. The default is the estate's canonical handbooks home (CON-13). Bounded: it must be the consumer's own pinned maintained_tools row (nen canon pin --source), so rulings and the matrix are read from one home; a value with no pinned row is missing-configuration, never a second home. hiraishin and kamui (zheref/hatsu#357, #356, shipped) reach it through bankai-rule's port-drift and the pair file it names. Read at the consumer's base tip, never its head (bankai-rule § 2).
values.question: Which handbooks repository carries this estate's port rulings?

values.describe: The directory inside workflow.port.handbooksRepo that holds the ports family: one directed pair file <from>--<to>.md per scenario pair and its INDEX.md (hatsu:bankai-rule § 4, rendered from templates/ports/). Read beside handbooks/stacks; the pair file is passed through nen canon resolve --always-load until zheref/nen#457 resolves it as a port handbook. hiraishin and kamui (zheref/hatsu#357, #356, shipped) reach it through bankai-rule's port-drift and the pair file it names. Bounded: one or more '/'-joined segments of [A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._-]* -- no empty, '.' or '..' segment, no leading '/' or './'; one trailing '/' is stripped, then the grammar applies, and the pair path is <rulingsDir>/<from>--<to>.md; the skill and scripts/port_rule_reserve.sh refuse anything else.
values.question: Which directory of the handbooks repository holds the port rulings?

values.describe: Whether this repository uses and expects its automated (AI) reviewers -- every bot in nen/gates.json reviewers[]. required: requested within round_policy's caps and expected; the merge prompt comes only at verified Ready or at PROCESS's sixth stop. optional: requested within the caps but not waited for; with nen pr ready failing exactly rounds-owed and hanten settled, the PR goes to the merge prompt on hanten's rounds, the not-ready verdict quoted verbatim. off: never requested (zero spend on requested reviewers; installed CI reviewer lanes still run and are turned off through the consumer's caller workflow -- PROCESS, Event-driven reviewer lanes), the same prompt as optional. Neither relaxes any other readiness row.
values.source: docs/WORKFLOW.md § 2 (aiReviewers); docs/PROCESS.md § Reviewer rounds and review threads, AI reviewers per consumer
values.question: Should this repository's AI reviewers be required (requested and waited for), optional (requested, never waited for) or off (never requested, no AI-reviewer spend)?

values.describe: One batch resolution per ask-once-per-run row of nen/decisions.json, applied only under a typed --idle go: default takes the row's starred option, hold parks the effort as parked:<row>, refuse ends that row's step unrun. A row the map does not name is hold (publish-offer refuse). A floor fails start at exit 1: publish-offer is always refuse; host-nen-link, harness-attribution-switch and missing-maintainer-choice are at most hold; default is refused on a row that stars no option. Read from the committed nen/workflow.json of the remote default branch only (origin/HEAD, else gh's defaultBranchRef; SEC-15), never HEAD or a ref HEAD's commit names, never the working tree; a default branch with no nen/workflow.json refuses start.
values.source: docs/ROSTER.md HR-5; nen/decisions.json ask-once-per-run rows (starred default, else hold); cleanup-plan held (an unattended remote branch deletion can close a stacked child), the five spec-* rows held (dowsing-chain is not an idle-run skill; spec-capture-scope and spec-converge-filing star an option), port-drift held (its answer is a permanent canon record, the maintainer's under the porting ruling, zheref/hatsu#354)

Wall-clock minutes an idle run may claim new efforts for, counted from the run manifest's startedAt; past it no effort is claimed and the rest park as parked:budget. Tokens an idle run may spend. Advisory and unread until zheref/nen#490 lands: no skill sums nen usage itself, and minutes remain the enforced bound.
